'''Censored regression models''' are a class of [[Regression analysis|models]] in which the [[Dependent and independent variables|dependent variable]] is [[Censoring (statistics)|censored]] above or below a certain threshold. A commonly used [[Likelihood function|likelihood-based]] model to accommodate to a censored sample is the [[Tobit model]],<ref>{{cite book |first=Richard |last=Breen |title=Regression Models : Censored, Samples Selected, or Truncated Data |location=Thousand Oaks |publisher=Sage |year=1996 |isbn=0-8039-5710-6 |chapter=The Tobit Model for Censored Data |pages=12–33 }}</ref> but [[Quantile regression|quantile]] and [[Nonparametric regression|nonparametric estimators]] have also been developed.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Moshe |last1=Buchinsky |first2=Jinyong |last2=Hahn |title=An Alternative Estimator for the Censored Quantile Regression Model |journal=[[Econometrica]] |volume=66 |issue=3 |year=1998 |pages=653–671 |doi=10.2307/2998578 |jstor=2998578 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first1=Arthur |last1=Lewbel |first2=Oliver |last2=Linton |title=Nonparametric Censored and Truncated Regression |journal=[[Econometrica]] |volume=70 |issue=2 |year=2002 |pages=765–779 |doi=10.1111/1468-0262.00304 |jstor=2692291 |url=https://researchonline.lse.ac.uk/id/eprint/2060/ }}</ref> These and other censored regression models are often confused with [[truncated regression model]]s. Truncated regression models are used for data where whole observations are missing so that the values for the dependent and the independent variables are unknown. Censored regression models are used for data where only the value for the dependent variable is unknown while the values of the independent variables are still available.

Censored dependent variables frequently arise in [[econometrics]]. A common example is [[labor supply]]. Data are frequently available on the hours worked by employees, and a labor supply model estimates the relationship between hours worked and characteristics of employees such as age, education and family status. However, such estimates undertaken using [[linear regression]] will be biased by the fact that for people who are unemployed it is not possible to observe the number of hours they would have worked had they had employment. Still we know age, education and family status for  those observations.
